response: In the case of Vivek Singh vs. Romani Singh, the court considered various factors while deciding the custody of the minor daughter, Saesha Singh. The court noted that Saesha had been living with her father from a tender age of 21 months and was happy in his company. Normally, these considerations would have prevailed upon the court to hold that custody of Saesha remain with the father. However, the court also took into account the other side of the picture. The court noted that for the first 21 months when the parties were living together, it was the mother who had nursed the child. The court also noted that the mother was forcibly deprived of the custody of Saesha from August 04, 2010, when she was forced to leave the matrimonial house. The mother had filed a petition seeking custody of the child and for appointment of her guardian within a few days of leaving the matrimonial house. The court also took into account the fact that the mother had not been able to reap the benefit of the custody of the child due to the interim orders passed in the instant appeal. The court noted that Saesha was 8 years and 3 months old at the time of the judgment and was very much attached to her father. The court also noted that Saesha had not seen, experienced, or lived the comfort of the company of her mother and was not in a position to comprehend that the grass on the other side may turn out to be greener. The court noted that only when she was exposed to that environment of living with her mother, that she would be in a position to properly evaluate as to whether her welfare lies more in the company of her mother or in the company of her father. The court also noted that as of today, the assessment and perception were one-sided. The court noted that few years ago, when the High Court passed the impugned judgment, the ground realities were different. The court noted that Saesha was at a crucial phase when there is a major shift in thinking ability which may help her to understand cause and effect better and think about the future. The court noted that she would need regular and frequent contact with each parent as well as shielding from parental hostility. The court noted that involvement of both parents in her life and regular school attendance are absolutely essential at this age for her personality development. The court noted that she would soon be able to establish her individual interests and preferences, shaped by her own individual personality as well as experience. The court noted that the factors in favor of the mother were weightier than those in favor of the father. The court noted that it was a fit case where the mother deserved a chance to have the custody of the child for the time being, at least for one year, and not merely visitation rights. The court ordered accordingly.
reference: The court considered the welfare of the minor child as the paramount consideration in deciding the custody. The court took into account the report of the Counsellor, Ms. Iti Kanungo, who interacted with the child and submitted a report stating that the child was more interested in living with her father. The court also heard the submissions of the counsel for both parties. The counsel for the appellant, Mr. V. Shekhar, emphasized that the father had taken care of the child since she was 21 months old and it was in her best interest to continue this arrangement. The counsel for the respondent, Ms. Geeta Luthra, argued that the respondent/mother was best person to take care of the child, especially considering her age and education needs. The court gave utmost serious consideration to the respective submissions and decided that the custody of the child should be given to the father, Vivek Singh.
